paragraphs.text: # The Shape of the World

The known world is vast, but interconnected. It can be easy to visualize the shape of Nevlos through an image, but for some it may be easier to understand the world through text. This document details the geography of Nevlos in a text-based format. It begins in the northwest corner of the world, proceeds southwards, before moving westwards, then northwards, and finally back westwards towards our starting location.
# The Dragon’s Shroud

Centered on the island of Elduin, the Dragon’s Shroud is a colossal, circular wall of dense, magical fog that separates those within it from those living beyond its borders. It was created by Syrath during the dragon’s final moments, with the intention of trapping Vaski, the last of the giants, within its confines.
# The Frost Gulf

Once connected to the open ocean, the mouth of this vast bay is now closed by the Dragon’s Shroud. It is a densely forested region, watered by moisture that gets blown eastward off the Dragon’s Shroud.
# Enua

Prior to the Enu Conquests of the 3rd century, this peninsula was known as Nethros. Its primary geographic features are two parallel mountain ranges (the Zada Mountains in the west and the Orosh Mountains in the northeast) that drain meltwater into the Lagetan Basin, a bread basket that has fed civilizations since long before the Doom.
# Ipherian Sea

Once united by the Ipherian Empire, this region splintered into successor states in the centuries following the Doom. Due to its location along key trade routes, it is a highly cosmopolitan region, especially the eastern coasts of Merovia and Agyros.
# Southern Ephria

Historically isolated from its northerly neighbors, the southern portion of Nevlos’ second, smaller continent is home to tropical rainforests and savannahs. With much of the region untouched by heavy human development, it is a refuge for some of Nevlos’ last great megafauna.
# Kovnia

This region’s dry, rocky landscape has forced its inhabitants to become dependent on trade to survive. Fortunately, its position between two maritime trading spheres (Ipheria in the west and Akál in the southeast) makes Kovnia the perfect region to facilitate such trade.
# Akál

Located off the southeastern coast of the continent, the Akali Archipelago is a large cluster of islands home to various seafaring peoples. Although generally decentralized, they were once united by the mighty seafaring empire of Tavilaga.
# The Central Empire

Dominating the eastern seaboard of the continent, the Central Empire is a multi-cultural hegemony spanning from the Yeosin Frontier in the north to the Sea of Akál in the south. Centered on a highly productive river basin called the Central Plain, this region has historically been one of the most densely populated places in the world.
# The Great Steppe

At the center of the continent is a massive, grassy plateau known as the Great Steppe. Since prehistory, it has been home to nomadic tribes who survived by hunting and herding. Today it is dotted with trading towns, which form a vast overland trade network connecting East and West.
